admission.justification: A held `j` can outrun the answer that brings the next family. "No later change in this tree" then stands beside a later change and tells the reader the walk is over when it is not. A status cleared by an update made while rendering comes back, because React can apply a queued status after that render. The rule is realized in the traversal hook and in the tree component, and a case on the hook alone and mounted cases guard it.

applicability: Select/end status for j/k and the previous/next real-change controls over the compact outline.
conditions: The status key consists of displayed order, All/Changed view and each shown row's family, selector and badge sequence.
The old message is gated out on the first render of a different key and cleared at commit; no state is updated while rendering.
Repeating the same message for the same key is a no-op; each new move may create its own status.
A select clears status; an end says no earlier/later change. The status appears beside the compact outline.
exclusions: No continuation-stop status or returned-roster-count identity.
The wording of end messages and the set of real-change stops remain separate contracts.
The retired rowsShown presentation and held-answer test are not current proof.
statement: The message of the last traversal move is shown only beside the rows the tree showed when it was said: once the tree has shown other rows the message is dropped and does not return when the tree shows the same rows again.
